chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Ghifari, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who sees the place (effect) of his speech on his deeds, would be scarce in his speech, except regarding what is meaningful'.
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of connecting one's speech to one's actions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the tradition of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this hadith links verbal restraint to spiritual integrity, suggesting that self-awareness of one's actions curbs idle talk. It reflects the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (consciousness of God) in speech, where the tongue serves as a mirror for the heart's alignment with divine will. This principle encourages believers to prioritize meaningful discourse over mere verbosity, fostering inner peace and clarity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Ghifary, from Ja’far Bin Ibrahim who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who sees the place (effect) of his speech on his deeds, would be scarce in his speech, except regarding what is meaningful’.
en.sarwar: 19. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Bakr ibn Salih form al-Ghaffari from Ja’far ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) say, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “If one can realize the effect of his words on his deeds, his words will decrease except for what he needs.’”
